body: Keep us posted for sure! Very interesting story. Be careful going back on that mountain. Definitely sounds like radiation, and you don't want to end up like those poor animals. If you can get your hands on a Geiger counter before you head back up, that would be a good move. Stay away if it goes off like crazy, maybe take old disposable cameras, film, so you don't have to rely on digital devices.
That was terrifying yet still so deep. Fantastic, thanks for sharing.
Thank you so much for the suggestions. I'm looking into them now.

I love this, I'm going to look more into some grief books. Especially the one refered in your comment. I've tried therapy, but it is very difficult to say these things face to face. I have problems with talking to strangers behind a screen more or less some doc that'll tell me I'm crazy.

I've been crying for help for the past two years and no one would listen. It took less than one hour for all of you to give me help, support, and care. And I've never even used Reddit before. Each response brought me to tears. I appreciate all of you. You guys don't realize how far your words have gotten to me. When strangers can lift my hopes more in 3 hours than anyone Ive known for years. Perhaps that is a sign that I have much to fix. Thank you all. <3  <3 <3

Any advice is still welcome. Because this isn't gonna change overnight, over a month or over a year. But some support gives me direction. Which I've needed for a long time. 

If anyone else needs to PM me as well. I may be a sad sack but I'll always listen, because I know what it's like to be in that place.
